metaDescription: Five foldable rolling overbed tables compared by height range, fold style and tilt, to help you find one that stores away when the bed is not in use.
introParagraphs: A foldable overbed table earns its place by disappearing. A fixed hospital-style table can crowd a small bedroom, while a folding one tucks behind a door or under a bed frame once breakfast or the laptop session is over. The five picks here all roll on casters and adjust in height, and they differ mainly in how much of the table actually folds.

We evaluated them based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at height range, tabletop tilt, caster design and the fold. The SageNest runs from 28.7 to 42.5 in on a gas spring, the JOY worker from 27.95 to 40.55 in, and the COMHOMA and GTPLAYER from 25 to 36.5 in on a snap-lock. The Mount-It folds down to 6.25 in thick and arrives assembled, which is the strongest storage claim in the group.

Foldable models trade some rigidity for portability, so check how steady the table feels at your working height and lock the wheels before leaning on it. Weight limits are not stated for most of these listings, so keep loads modest and confirm with the seller if you plan to place anything heavy on top.

products.name: SageNest Foldable Rolling Overbed Table
specs: Usable on either side of bed
products.description:
The SageNest uses a pneumatic gas spring to move the table between 28.7 and 42.5 in, the tallest ceiling in this group. The tabletop tilts anywhere from 0 to 180 degrees with a one-touch control, so it can serve either side of a bed. Four hidden 360 degree casters keep the base low and quiet when it rolls.

The wide height range suits a high bed, a recliner or standing use at a desk. The listing mentions pre-drilled holes on the top for add-ons, and the low profile base slides under furniture. The listing does not state a weight limit or the exact tabletop size, so confirm both with the seller before buying for heavy loads, and lock all four casters whenever you lean on it.

Setting up is a matter of unfolding and adjusting the gas spring lever. Against the COMHOMA at 25 to 36.5 in, it lifts roughly six inches higher. Against the JOY worker at 27.95 to 40.55 in, it adds a little more reach at the top while lacking the folding base.
products.bestFor: People who want the tallest range and a full tilt top on a quiet, low-profile base.

products.name: JOY worker Foldable Portable Overbed Table
specs: Use on either side of bed
products.description:
The JOY worker folds both the tabletop and the base, which the listing contrasts with tables that only fold the top. That means it can slide into a narrow gap beside a wardrobe or under a bed. A gas spring handles the height from 27.95 to 40.55 in, and the tabletop tilts stepless over 180 degrees when you squeeze the handle.

Stepless tilt lets you pick any angle for reading or a tablet instead of a few preset notches. The folding base is the main storage advantage, though every hinge is another part to check for firm locking. As with the others, the listing gives no weight limit, so keep loads moderate and ask the seller for a figure if you plan to rest anything heavy on it.

It rolls on casters and adjusts one-handed, so little bending is needed. Compared with the Mount-It, which folds to 6.25 in thick, the JOY worker adds tilt and a gas spring. Compared with the SageNest at 28.7 to 42.5 in, its top height is about two inches lower but its base folds away.
products.bestFor: Small bedrooms where the whole table needs to fold flat for storage.

products.name: Mount-It Folding Adjustable Overbed Table
specs: Use at bed, couch or recliner
products.description:
The Mount-It collapses to just 6.25 in thick, which is the slimmest stored size claimed here. It arrives fully assembled, so you unfold it from the box and use it, with no tools or hardware. The listing frames it as a rolling table for the bed, the couch or a recliner.

The simple folding frame is the reason it is easy to put away, closet storage included. The listing does not supply the height range, tabletop size or weight limit, so those need confirming with the seller before you buy, especially if the bed is tall. Simpler mechanics also mean fewer features, with no gas spring or tilt claimed in the listing.

It suits occasional use more than daily heavy use. Compared with the JOY worker, it gives up the tilt top in exchange for a flatter fold. Compared with the COMHOMA, it advertises the thinner stored size but gives fewer measurements.
products.bestFor: Occasional users who need a table that stores almost flat in a closet or behind a door.

products.name: COMHOMA Adjustable Overbed Table with Lockable Wheels
products.description:
The COMHOMA adjusts through a snap-lock system from 25 to 36.5 in, which includes lower settings than the gas spring tables. The tabletop folds up to 90 degrees to save floor space, and four swivel wheels lock to hold it in place. The listing frames it as both a bedside table and a rolling laptop desk.

A lower floor of 25 in suits a low bed, a sofa or a low armchair, and the snap-lock holds each setting without a spring. The snap-lock steps in discrete jumps, and the top only folds, so the base stays full size. Weight limit and tabletop dimensions are not given in the listing.

It rolls easily and parks firmly once the wheels are locked. It matches the GTPLAYER on height and fold, but the SageNest rises nearly six inches higher at 42.5 in. Choose it for lower seating more than for tall beds.
products.bestFor: Low beds, sofas and armchairs where a lower starting height of 25 in helps.

Top folds up to 90 degrees to free floor space
Snap-lock holds notches with no gas spring
cons: Base does not fold, only the top
Weight limit is not stated in the listing

products.name: GTPLAYER Foldable Mobile Rolling Laptop Table
products.description:
The GTPLAYER pairs a 24 in tabletop with the same 25 to 36.5 in snap-lock range as the COMHOMA. The top folds up to 90 degrees to clear floor space in a small room, and four swivel wheels lock to hold it. It is described as a small standing desk that doubles as an overbed table.

A 24 in top is narrower than many overbed tables, so it fits a laptop or a tray but not a full spread of dishes and papers. It is easy to tuck in a tight corner. The listing says nothing of tilt or weight limit, so it is a plain sliding surface.

Compared with the COMHOMA, the specs read nearly the same, with the 24 in width being the clearest distinction. Compared with the SageNest at 28.7 to 42.5 in, it does not reach standing height. Choose it where space is tight and loads are light.
products.bestFor: Small rooms and light loads such as a laptop, a book or a meal tray.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The table must slide over your bed or chair without touching, and still reach a comfortable height for eating or typing. The COMHOMA and GTPLAYER start at 25 in, the JOY worker at 27.95 in and the SageNest at 28.7 in. If your bed is tall or you sit upright, look for a top end near 40 in, such as the SageNest at 42.5 in. Measure the bed height before choosing.

Folding top only, folding base and folding both are three different storage experiences. The COMHOMA and GTPLAYER fold only the top to 90 degrees, the JOY worker folds both the top and the base, and the Mount-It collapses to 6.25 in thick. If you plan to store it daily, choose a full fold. If it stays at the bedside, a folding top is enough.

A tilting top turns a flat surface into a reading or tablet stand. The SageNest tilts 0 to 180 degrees with one-touch control, and the JOY worker tilts stepless over 180 degrees. The COMHOMA and GTPLAYER only fold up to 90 degrees. Choose tilt if you read in bed, and skip it if you only eat there.

A gas spring gives smooth one-handed height changes, while a snap-lock holds fixed notches. The SageNest and JOY worker use gas springs, and the COMHOMA and GTPLAYER use snap-locks. A gas spring is easier for weak hands, and a snap-lock has no spring to wear. Pick based on how often and how easily you change heights.

A rolling table is only safe to lean on when it is locked. The COMHOMA and GTPLAYER list four lockable swivel wheels, and the SageNest has four hidden 360 degree casters. Check that the wheels actually lock before placing a laptop or hot drink on it. Smooth carpet and hardwood roll differently, so test the table on your own floor.

Surface area decides what fits: the GTPLAYER top is 24 in wide, which suits a laptop but not a full meal setup. Weight limits are not stated for most of these listings, so keep loads modest and ask the seller for a figure before putting anything heavy on top. The Mount-It lists no top dimension in our product data. Confirm size and capacity before buying.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the low and high ends of each table, from the 25 in start of the COMHOMA and GTPLAYER to the 42.5 in top of the SageNest. A wider span scored better for fitting different beds and chairs. This is based on product specs and buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fold and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how much each table shrinks when put away. The Mount-It at 6.25 in thick and the JOY worker with a folding base lead here, while the COMHOMA and GTPLAYER fold only their tops. Real closet fit depends on your space.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tilt and adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We assessed tilt range and lift type, noting the SageNest at 0 to 180 degrees and the JOY worker with stepless 180 degree tilt. Gas spring tables earned credit for smooth one-hand changes. Snap-lock tables were credited for simplicity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mobility and locking
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at casters and whether they lock, including the four lockable swivel wheels on the COMHOMA and GTPLAYER. A table that rolls easily but will not park firmly was marked down. We did not evaluate floors or surfaces.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing completeness
howWeEvaluated.description: Because several listings omit weight limits and tabletop sizes, we flagged those gaps for each pick. The Mount-It lacks a height range in our data, while the GTPLAYER states its 24 in width. More complete details increased confidence.

faq.q: Which foldable overbed table folds the smallest?
faq.a: The Mount-It collapses to 6.25 in thick, the slimmest figure listed. The JOY worker folds both its top and its base, which also stores compactly. The COMHOMA and GTPLAYER fold only the top, so their base stays full size.

faq.q: How do I choose between the SageNest and the JOY worker?
faq.a: The SageNest reaches 42.5 in and tilts 0 to 180 degrees, while the JOY worker covers 27.95 to 40.55 in and folds its base. Pick the SageNest for a tall bed or standing use. Pick the JOY worker when storage space is the limit.

faq.q: Do these tables have a weight limit?
faq.a: Most of the listings here do not state one, so we cannot give a figure. Keep loads modest, avoid leaning your body weight on the table, and ask the seller for a rating before placing anything heavy on top. Always lock the wheels first.

faq.q: Is a folding table less stable than a fixed one?
faq.a: It can be, because hinges and folding joints add flex compared with a solid welded frame. Stability also depends on the height setting and where the load sits. Keep the table close to the bed, lock the casters and check the folding locks before use.

faq.q: Will it fit under my bed?
faq.a: The SageNest has a low-profile base with hidden casters, and the JOY worker has a folding base. Measure the clearance under your bed frame against the base height in the listing. Remember the table needs to straddle the bed, so the base sits on the floor beside it.

Gas springs can lose lift over time, especially with heavy loads or years of daily use. A snap-lock has no spring but holds only fixed notches. For occasional use, either is fine, and for daily changes a gas spring is more convenient.

faq.q: Can I use these as a standing desk?
faq.a: The SageNest reaches 42.5 in and the JOY worker 40.55 in, which can serve as light standing use for some people. The COMHOMA and GTPLAYER top out at 36.5 in, which is closer to a seated height. Fit depends on your own height, so check before relying on it.
